clauses.reason: Whole order (two numbered paragraphs of the held text): the closing applies to Monday, November 25, 1963 only. Terminated by its own terms at the close of that day, recorded as 1963-11-25. No amendment, supersession or revocation is held, so there is no earlier end.

research_rationale:
EO 11128 (November 23, 1963, signed by Lyndon B. Johnson, printed at 28 FR 12609), read in full in the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11128.txt (machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, graded original_representation_unverified and counted as an official original; the OCR prints the number as 111 28 but the number, title and date agree with the census register; I did not inspect the PDF page images). Content: paragraph 1 orders all Executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies, including their field services, closed on Monday, November 25, 1963, as a mark of respect for President John Fitzgerald Kennedy; paragraph 2 says the order does not apply to offices and installations, or parts of them, in the Department of State, the Department of Defense or other departments and agencies that the heads determine should remain open for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons. First end: by its own terms the closing covers the single day named, Monday, November 25, 1963, and the order ends at the close of that day; recorded as 1963-11-25. The order uses no until wording, so there is no inclusive or exclusive reading beyond the day itself. Later events: none found. The three selected machine searches have no hit for this order; a citation search of the 33,118 held order texts under jobs/*/output/texts (clause-drafts excluded) for the forms Executive Order 11128, Order No. 11128 and E.O. 11128 finds nothing; I also read the held text of EO 12553 (51 FR 7237) and its table of revoked orders does not print the number 11128. A later revocation would fall after the own-terms end in any event. The standing disclosure that this order rests on a Federal Register OCR text layer and not on an authenticated original applies.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transition or pay language and does not declare a holiday for leave or pay purposes. Whatever pay or leave consequences followed from the closing depend on other statutes and rules and are not a continuing command of this order after November 25, 1963.
